# Configuration reference

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_config_docs.py — do not edit by hand. -->

Every setting Edibl understands. This table is generated from the same
inventory the application validates against, so it cannot drift.

## Precedence

Highest wins:

1. **Explicit config** passed to `create_app()` (tests, embedding).
2. **Home Assistant add-on options** (`/data/options.json`).
3. **Environment variables** (`EDIBL_*`, or `EDIBL_*_FILE` for secrets).
4. **Built-in defaults.**

Home Assistant options outrank the environment because, inside the add-on,
options.json is the only surface an operator can edit — if the environment
won, toggling a switch in the HA UI would silently do nothing. Outside Home
Assistant the file does not exist, so the environment is authoritative.

An empty environment variable (`EDIBL_AI_PROVIDER=`) means *unset*, and falls
through to the default rather than failing validation. The same applies to a
cleared field in the Home Assistant UI, which writes an empty string.

## Validation

Configuration is validated once at startup, before the database is opened
and before any port is bound. Invalid configuration prints **every** problem
and refuses to start — it never surfaces later as a request-time 500.

Booleans accept `1 true yes on` / `0 false no off` (any case). Anything else
is an error: an unrecognised value is never silently treated as false.

Check a deployment without starting it — this also prints which settings are
non-default and where each came from, which is the fastest way to answer
"but I set that option":

```bash
docker compose run --rm app python3 -m app.config_check
```

## Settings

### Storage

| Variable | Type | Default | Secret | HA option | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `EDIBL_DATA_DIR` | string | `./data` | no | — | Directory for the SQLite database, uploads and persisted secrets. |
| `EDIBL_DATABASE_URL` | string | `_(empty)_` | **yes** | `database_url` | Full SQLAlchemy URL. Blank = SQLite inside DATA_DIR. Postgres is supported: postgresql+psycopg://user:pass@host:5432/dbname. Supports `EDIBL_DATABASE_URL_FILE`. |
| `EDIBL_MIGRATE_FROM_SQLITE` | boolean | `false` | no | `migrate_from_sqlite` | One-shot: when DATABASE_URL points at an EMPTY Postgres and a local SQLite database exists, copy the SQLite data across at startup. |
| `EDIBL_USE_SHARED_POSTGRES` | boolean | `false` | no | `use_shared_postgres` | Home Assistant only: discover the Shared PostgreSQL add-on and use a database it provisions for Edibl. Ignored when DATABASE_URL is set. |
| `EDIBL_POSTGRES_PROVISION_TOKEN` | string | `_(empty)_` | **yes** | `postgres_provision_token` | Token for the Shared PostgreSQL add-on's provisioning API. Blank auto-obtains it via discovery. |

### Security

| Variable | Type | Default | Secret | HA option | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `EDIBL_SECRET_KEY` | string | `_(empty)_` | **yes** | — | JWT signing key. Blank = generated once and persisted in DATA_DIR. Deliberately has no add-on option: a key that changed per boot would log every user out and void every API token on each restart. Supports `EDIBL_SECRET_KEY_FILE`. |
| `EDIBL_JWT_HOURS` | enum/int | `72` | no | — | How long an issued token stays valid, in hours. |
| `EDIBL_DISABLE_AUTH` | boolean | `false` | no | `disable_auth` | Bind every request to a single local user. ONLY safe behind an authenticating proxy such as Home Assistant ingress. |
| `EDIBL_ALLOW_REGISTRATION` | boolean | `true` | no | — | Allow anyone who can reach the app to create an account. |
| `EDIBL_MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH` | enum/int | `8` | no | — | Minimum password length enforced on register / change-password. |
| `EDIBL_WORKER_ENABLED` | boolean | `true` | no | — | Run the in-process background-job worker thread (async AI tooling). |
| `EDIBL_SEED_DEFAULTS` | boolean | `true` | no | — | Seed a new database with the default locations, units and categories. |

### Network & proxy

| Variable | Type | Default | Secret | HA option | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `EDIBL_PORT` | enum/int | `7746` | no | — | HTTP port for the app. |
| `EDIBL_CORS_ORIGINS` | list | `_(empty)_` | no | — | Comma-separated origins allowed to make credentialed cross-origin requests. Empty = same-origin only (correct for normal deployments). |
| `EDIBL_PROXY_HOPS` | enum/int | `0` | no | — | How many reverse proxies sit in front. 0 = do not trust X-Forwarded-* headers at all. |
| `EDIBL_RATELIMIT_ENABLED` | boolean | `true` | no | — | Enable request rate limiting (disabled automatically under tests). |

### LLM assistant

| Variable | Type | Default | Secret | HA option | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `EDIBL_LLM_PROVIDER` | enum/int | `_(empty)_` | no | `llm_provider` | Which LLM backend the assistant uses. Blank = rules only. |
| `EDIBL_LLM_BASE_URL` | string | `_(empty)_` | no | `llm_base_url` | Base URL of the LLM server (local Ollama, an OpenAI-compatible gateway, or blank for the provider default). |
| `EDIBL_LLM_API_KEY` | string | `_(empty)_` | **yes** | `llm_api_key` | API key for the configured LLM provider. Supports `EDIBL_LLM_API_KEY_FILE`. |
| `EDIBL_LLM_MODEL` | string | `_(empty)_` | no | `llm_model` | Model name for the configured LLM provider. |
| `EDIBL_LLM_AGENT_ID` | string | `_(empty)_` | no | `llm_agent_id` | Only for the `homeassistant` provider: which HA conversation agent to target (e.g. conversation.ollama). Blank = HA's default agent. |
| `EDIBL_LLM_TIMEOUT` | enum/int | `60` | no | — | Per-request timeout for LLM provider calls, in seconds. |
| `EDIBL_LLM_MAX_STEPS` | enum/int | `6` | no | — | Maximum tool-calling rounds the assistant may take per message. |
| `EDIBL_AI_CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD` | number | `0.8` | no | — | Auto-categorization: a proposal at/above this model-reported confidence is applied automatically; below it goes to review. |
| `EDIBL_OLLAMA_SEARCH_KEY` | string | `_(empty)_` | **yes** | `ollama_search_key` | Ollama API key (ollama.com) for the hosted web search used to write product descriptions. Blank = enrichment is off. Supports `EDIBL_OLLAMA_SEARCH_KEY_FILE`. |

| Variable | Type | Default | Secret | HA option | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `EDIBL_MCP_ENABLED` | boolean | `true` | no | `mcp_enabled` | Run the MCP server so Home Assistant Assist can use Edibl as a tool. |
| `EDIBL_MCP_HOST` | string | `0.0.0.0` | no | — | Bind address for the MCP server. |
| `EDIBL_MCP_PORT` | enum/int | `7767` | no | — | Port for the MCP server (SSE). |
| `EDIBL_MCP_API` | string | `_(empty)_` | no | — | Backend API URL the MCP server calls. Blank = derived from PORT. |
| `EDIBL_MCP_API_TOKEN` | string | `_(empty)_` | **yes** | — | Token the MCP server uses when app auth is enabled. Supports `EDIBL_MCP_API_TOKEN_FILE`. |
| `EDIBL_MCP_SERVER_TOKEN` | string | `_(empty)_` | **yes** | `mcp_server_token` | Bearer token Home Assistant must present to reach the MCP server. Supports `EDIBL_MCP_SERVER_TOKEN_FILE`. |
| `EDIBL_MCP_EXPOSE_EXTERNAL` | boolean | `false` | no | `mcp_expose_external` | Reach the MCP server from OUTSIDE Home Assistant. When on, every request must present a Full- or MCP-scoped API key, and the server refuses to start until such a key exists — so it is never open. |

## Security notes

- **`EDIBL_SECRET_KEY`** must be at least 32 characters when
  authentication is enabled, and known placeholders are rejected outright.
  Leave it unset and Edibl generates one **once** and persists it to
  `$EDIBL_DATA_DIR/.secret_key` (mode 0600). Back that file up with your data:
  losing it logs everyone out and voids every issued API token. It has no
  add-on option on purpose — a key that changed per boot would do exactly
  that on every restart.
- **`EDIBL_DISABLE_AUTH=true` binds every request to one local user.** It is
  correct behind Home Assistant ingress and wrong anywhere else. Combining it
  with `EDIBL_CORS_ORIGINS` is refused outright, because that would let any
  listed website drive the API as that user.
- **CORS is same-origin by default.** The SPA is served by the app itself, so
  no cross-origin access is needed. Only add origins for a separate frontend
  (e.g. the Vite dev server at `http://localhost:5173`). `*` is refused.
- **`X-Forwarded-*` headers are ignored** unless `EDIBL_PROXY_HOPS` says how
  many proxies are in front. Trusting them by default would let any client
  spoof its IP and evade rate limiting.
- **`EDIBL_MCP_EXPOSE_EXTERNAL`** makes the MCP server reachable from outside
  Home Assistant. It is fail-closed: the server refuses to start unless a
  Full- or MCP-scoped API key already exists, so it is never open.
- **`EDIBL_DATABASE_URL` is a secret** — it embeds the database password.
  It is redacted everywhere Edibl reports configuration.

## Deployment support

- **Docker secrets**: any setting marked `Supports EDIBL_*_FILE` can be read
  from a file instead, e.g. `EDIBL_SECRET_KEY_FILE=/run/secrets/edibl_key`.
- **Home Assistant add-on**: set options in the add-on's Configuration tab.
  The `HA option` column above gives the key name.
